decisions.reason: Having survived several years after launch and fitting closely with the core formwork portfolio, it likely remains at least near aspiration levels, so an expanding firm with R&D slack would keep it unless recent sales had clearly disappointed.

Although its lower visibility suggests somewhat more uncertainty, it supports the firm's automation and integrated factory-system strategy, so management would usually retain it while its contribution remains acceptable relative to aspirations.

As a close-to-core product line that can complement broader system sales, it is more likely to be kept than dropped, with withdrawal becoming more likely only if its standalone and cross-selling results have fallen below target.

Its strong fit with the established magnetic formwork offering and earlier dedicated presentation indicate strategic relevance, so behavioral-theory management would normally continue it absent clear evidence of underperformance.
